title: CRLR/90/2006 of M/S MAHESWARI CHITS PVT. LTD. and ANO Vs STATE and ANO

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.90 of 2006
M/s Maheswari Chits Pvt. Ltd.
& another ... Revisionists
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & another ... Respondents
AND
Criminal Revision No.91 of 2006
 M/s Maheswari Chits Pvt. Ltd.
& another ... Revisionists
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & another ... Respondents
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. List revised. Case called out twice. No one is present for
the revisionists as well as for respondent no.2. Heard Mr. P. S.
Danu, Brief Holder for the State.
2. Criminal Revision No.90/2006 pertains to a complaint
filed by respondent no.2/Anwar Ahmad under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instrument Act, as a cheque No.326863 amounting to
Rs.95,000/- issued in his favour by the revisionist was
dishonoured by the bank on 15.04.1998 due to insufficiency of
funds. Criminal Revision No.91/2006 pertains to a complaint
filed by respondent no.2/Anwar Ahmad under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instrument Act, as the second cheque No.326864
amounting to Rs.24,000/- issued in his favour by the revisionist
was dishonoured by the bank on 15.04.1998 due to insufficiency
of funds. In both matters, the drawee (remitter) and payee were
the present revisionist and respondent no.2 respectively.
However, both these matters were decided separately by the trial
court by separate judgments of common date i.e. 09.11.2005.
3. So far as the first cheque No.326863 amounting to
Rs.95,000/- is concerned, the trial court convicted the
revisionists under Section 138/141 of N.I. Act and sentenced to
undergo rigorous imprisonment of one year and a fine of
Rs.5000/- and the revisionists were directed to pay a sum of

-2-
Rs.1,85,000/-. So far as the second cheque No.326864
amounting to Rs.24,000/- is concerned, the trial court convicted
the revisionists under Section 138/141 of the N.I. Act and
sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment of one year and a
fine of Rs.5000/-. In default of payment of fine, the revisionists
have to further undergo simple imprisonment for six months.
The revisionists were directed to pay a sum of Rs.43,000/- to the
complainant as compensation.
4. When the matter came to the Sessions Judge, though the
conviction against the revisionists was upheld, the sentence was
modified to the extent of payment of fine of Rs.5,000/-. In other
words, the sentence of imprisonment of one year as awarded by
the trial court was set aside. The Sessions Judge also affirmed
compensation of Rs.43,000/- & Rs.1,85,000/- to be paid to
complainant by the revisionists.
5. Since in both the matters, the drawee (remitter) and payee
were the same, hence both revisions are being decided together
by this common judgment.
6. Respondent no.2/Anwar Ahmad filed a complaint against
the revisionists before the Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar with the
allegations that the revisionists gave him two cheques No.326863
& 326864 amounting to Rs.95,000/- & Rs.24,000/-,
respectively. The respondent no.2/complainant approached the
bank, but the cheques were dishonoured by the bank on
15.04.1998 due to insufficiency of funds. Subsequently, two
separate notices dated 27.04.1998 were issued to the revisionists,
which were refused to accept by the revisionists. Thereafter, the
complainant was constrained to file two separate complaints
under Section 138 of the N.I. Act before the Magistrate.
7. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined as
many as three witnesses. V. P. Singh, who was the Manager of

-3-
Allahabad Bank, Roorkee Branch, was examined as PW1. He
states that the revisionist has an account in the Allahabad Bank,
Roorkee Branch since 1994. He has verified the signature of the
revisionist on the cheque in question and there was only a
balance of Rs.182/- in the revisionist's account. Anwar Ahmad,
who was the complainant in this case, was examined as PW2. He
narrated the prosecution as has been stated in the complaint.
Harnek Singh, who was the Joint Manager of Bank of Baroda,
Roorkee Branch, was examined as PW3. He states that the
complainant has an account in the Bank of Baroda, Roorkee and
the cheque issued by the revisionist drawn on the Allahabad
Bank was received in the Bank of Baroda and the said cheque was
sent to the Allahabad Bank for clearance. He states that the
cheque was dishonoured due to insufficient funds.
8. The trial court after hearing the parties convicted the
revisionist under Section 138/141 of the N.I. Act and sentenced to
undergo rigorous imprisonment of one year and a fine of
Rs.5000/-. In default of payment of fine, the revisionists have to
further undergo simple imprisonment for six months. The
revisionists were directed to pay a sum of Rs.1,85,000/- to the
complainant as compensation.
9. Feeling aggrieved, the revisionists filed an appeal before
the Sessions Judge, which was partly allowed and suspended the
sentence awarded to the revisionists. It was held by the Sessions
Judge that the parameters contained under Section 138 of the
N.I. Act are fully applicable in the present case.
10. Aggrieved by both orders of the court below, the
revisionists have filed present revisions.
11. This Court has perused the impugned judgments and finds
that both the impugned judgments are well reasoned. This Court
finds that valid reasons have been assigned by the trial court for

-4-
convicting the revisionists based on evidence which is absolutely
convincing. Therefore, there is no anomaly in the impugned
judgments. No interference is required in this matter. The
revisions fail and are hereby dismissed accordingly.
12. Interim order dated 25.05.2006 stands vacated. Lower
Court record be sent back. Registrar General is directed to send a
copy of this order to the court concerned for compliance.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dated 23rd April, 2013
Rawat
